status: MP15 MOTOR HOLDER v1 - desk stand for the MKS SERVO42D motor with the MP6 cycloid reducer fixed on its face. Axis horizontal. Sizes here are author choices unless a source is named; motor / reducer sizes are read from their own files (sources), fits only from the ledger (fits_from). R1 (2026-11-05) = output review dispositions (.dev/mp15-evidence/review-r1-disposition.md)
decision: .dev/mp15-evidence/user-decisions-mp15.json - user 2026-11-04 question box '따로 모터 받침 (권장)' (holder wrapping the motor body, screw holes in its base; reducer parts unchanged) -> 2026-11-05 unit number 'MP15'
frame: x = motor axis (motor front face x = 0, motor body toward +x, reducer toward -x) · z = up (desk / print bed = z 0) · y = across. Both STLs are built in the assembled pose: the holder pose = its print pose (base on the bed); the bar STL sits on the motor top (z = motor top) and print_prep_holder.py only lowers it to the bed

sources.note: read only - the generator and the checks read these files and record their sha256; nothing is copied by hand except connector_front below (checked against the J5 file). The connector height / width / centre are used only for the preview picture

fits_from.note: M3 heat-set insert hole (confirmed 4.0) and M3 clearance (placeholder 3.4) - never written here

axis_height_note: reducer outer radius 39 -> its lowest point 16 above the desk (11 above the base top) - room for fingers under the housing. The two front base holes (x -6) sit under the housing edge: screw them before the motor goes in

cradle.note: U channel under the motor body. Front x 0.3 = the reducer base plate's back face (x 0, Ø78 flat) is the backward stop (0.3 play) - the two lower cap screw heads get pockets (keepout.cap_screw_head), the two upper heads are above the wall top. Rear x 26 = 3.0 in front of the motor's own 6-pin connector (29 from the face, on one body face) so a forward slip of up to 3.0 meets nothing and the connector may face any side; the driver behind (wider than the body) stays clear. Floor = axis_height - frame / 2 (the motor rests on it); wall top = motor top - clamp_gap so the bar presses the motor, not the walls, while the frame is up to clamp_gap smaller than the ledger value (not a tightening stop - tighten lightly)

bar.note: clamp bar across the motor top, two M3 button-head screws into inserts in the wall tops. 20 x 8 (R1: 14 x 5 could crack at the motor edge when tightened). The counterbore lets the M3 x 10 on hand reach 4.0 into the 5.7 insert; M3 x 12 = full 5.7 (tip 6.0 above the 8.0 hole floor). Tighten lightly; print it flat, infill 100 % if set per object in the slicer window

inserts.note: insert = BOM R06 (M3 x 5.7 x 4.2, hole 4.0 from the ledger). Centre in the middle of the wall: 2.0 to each face in the 4.0 hole, about 1.9 around the 4.2 insert. x 15 keeps the bar (x 5 - 25) behind the upper cap screw heads (x <= 3.0) and 4 in front of the connector

base.note: flat flange for 4 screws (M4 or 4 mm wood screws) into a board or the desk, or clamps on its edge

cap_screw_head.note: cycloid screws.cap = M3 x 30 from under the base into the cap inserts, holes at cap_screw radius on the 45 deg diagonals (the motor bolt diagonals, so the same for every 90 deg way the reducer goes on). Head = ISO 4762 socket 5.5 x 3.0 or ISO 7380 button 5.7 x 1.65 (BOM R08) - the larger of each. Pockets (radius + pocket_gap, to height + pocket_depth_gap) in the holder front for the heads below the wall top

print.note: holder on its base (U opens upward - no support), bar flat

check_note: C2 side clearance band = the designed clearance per side measured against the ledger frame (it does not test the real frame - only a caliper reading does; a real frame up to +0.7 still slides in, up to -1.0 still clamps). C5 clamp band = the bar meets the motor top first. Hole diameters are area-equivalent from fine STL sections (read a little under the design value)
